mainTopic: Why one שליח is believed when he says בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, and the debate between רבה and רבא over the reason
overview: This amud continues the discussion of a שליח who brings a גט from overseas and says בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. The גמרא explains that חכמים trusted a single שליח because of עיגונא, the worry that a woman could be left stuck in her marriage. It asks whether this is really a קולא, since the husband could contest a גט backed by only one witness. The answer is that the גט is handed over in front of two or three people, so the שליח checks carefully and will not risk shaming himself. Following רבא's reason, that witnesses for קיום are hard to find, the גמרא asks why two witnesses are not needed. It answers with רבי שמעון בן לקיש's teaching: by Torah law a signed document needs no קיום at all, so חכמים were free to relax their own rule because of עיגונא. The גמרא then sets רבה and רבא against each other. Each explains why he rejects the other's reason, and each explains the wording of the משנה according to his own view. The amud ends by asking which תנא matches רבה's view, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages were lenient because of עיגונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: one שליח is believed because חכמים were lenient, so that women would not be left as עגונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the worry that she would be left stuck in her marriage, the Sages were lenient with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it already started: we accept one שליח, and do not demand two witnesses, because חכמים were lenient to prevent עיגונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a matter of marriage, a דבר שבערוה, needs two witnesses. Here חכמים made an exception and accepted one שליח, because otherwise many women could never be sure they were divorced and would be unable to remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of being an עגונה, a woman stuck in her marriage and unable to remarry
They were lenient
The Sages, חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: The concern for עיגונא is a basic principle that shows up across הלכות גיטין and קידושין. The next steps test whether this ruling really is a leniency at all.

phrases.english: Because of the concern of being left a deserted wife, the Sages were lenient with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם עִיגּוּנָא אַקִּילוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the earlier question of why one שליח is enough, even though a דבר שבערוה normally needs two witnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic leniency based on a policy concern (preventing עיגונא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since marriage matters need two witnesses, we should require two here as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים deliberately relaxed the rule and accepted one שליח, so that women would not become עגונות.

steps.title: Isn't believing one witness actually a stringency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim of leniency: with two witnesses the husband could not contest the גט, but with one he can come and invalidate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a leniency? It is a stringency! If you require two witnesses for it, the husband cannot come, contest it, and invalidate it. With only one witness, the husband can come, contest it, and invalidate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that accepting one שליח helps the woman. It argues that it actually puts her at risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two witnesses, the husband's word cannot stand against them, so the גט is secure. With only one שליח, the husband's word stands against the שליח's word, so he can contest the גט. The woman might remarry and then lose her divorce, which is worse for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A leniency
A stringency
Contests, challenges the validity
Invalidates

phrases.english: Is this a leniency?! It is a stringency!
For if you require two witnesses for it,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעֵר וּפָסֵיל לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: the husband does not come, contest, and invalidate it;

phrases.aramaic: חַד – אָתֵי בַּעַל וּמְעַרְעֵר וּפָסֵיל לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: with one, the husband comes, contests, and invalidates it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קוּלָּא הוּא?! חוּמְרָא הוּא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the description of the ruling in Step 1 as a leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that accepting one שליח is a קולא because of עיגונא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single witness leaves the גט open to the husband's challenge, while two witnesses would protect it. So the ruling actually hurts the woman.

steps.title: The שליח checks carefully because the גט is given in public
steps.stepSummary: Since the גט must be handed over in front of two or three people, the שליח is careful from the start and will not risk bringing a flawed גט, so the husband's challenge is not a real worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said: In front of how many people does he give it to her? רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא disagree. One said in front of two, and one said in front of three. So from the beginning the שליח checks carefully, and he will not bring harm on himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the גט is given in front of a group, the שליח makes sure everything is right from the start, so the husband will not really be able to undo it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליח knows he will hand over the גט publicly, in front of two (or three) people. If it later turns out to be invalid, he will be shamed, so he checks carefully. That makes a successful challenge by the husband unlikely, so accepting one שליח is still a real קולא.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of how many people
He gives it (the גט) to her
He is certainly careful, he checks thoroughly
To harm or discredit himself

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
phrases.notes: "The Master" is the גמרא's way of quoting an earlier teaching; here it quotes the dispute that follows.

phrases.english: In front of how many does he give it to her?
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Chanina disagree;
one said: in front of two,
and one said: in front of three;
so from the start he checks carefully,
and he will not come to bring harm on himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: בִּפְנֵי כַּמָּה נוֹתְנוֹ לָהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality removes the feared risk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only one שליח, the husband can easily overturn the גט, so the ruling hurts the woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the גט is delivered publicly, the שליח verifies it carefully, so a challenge by the husband is unlikely and the ruling remains a real leniency.
steps.whatToRemember: Accepting one שליח is a true קולא for the woman, because the public handing over of the גט makes the שליח careful.

steps.title: According to רבא, why not require two witnesses as with any document?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the reason for saying בפני נכתב is that witnesses to confirm the signatures are not available. If so, the שליח's statement is a confirmation of a document, which normally needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, who said the reason is that there are no witnesses available to confirm it, let us require two, just like the confirming of ordinary documents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same 'why only one?' question, but this time according to רבא's reason for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the שליח's statement takes the place of the usual confirmation of the signatures, קיום שטרות. In normal cases, confirming a שטר needs two witnesses. So, the גמרא argues, two should be needed here too.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose view is that בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם is said because confirming witnesses are hard to find
Available, easily found
To confirm it (the signatures on the document)
Confirming the validity of legal documents in court
In general, ordinary

phrases.english: And according to Rava, who said
it is because there are no witnesses available to confirm it,
let us require two,
just as with confirming ordinary documents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרָבָא דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier approach to רבא's reason, and asks the same question of why one שליח is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: Accepting one שליח according to רבא's reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the שליח's statement serves as confirmation of the document, it should follow the normal rule for confirming documents, which requires two witnesses.

steps.title: One witness is believed in matters of איסור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a single witness is believed in matters of איסור, and that applies here.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness is believed in matters of prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's question with a known rule: in matters of איסור, one witness is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary documents usually deal with money, and that needs two witnesses. A גט decides an איסור question, whether the woman is permitted to remarry, and there one witness is trusted. So the normal two-witness rule for documents does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness
Is believed, trusted
Matters of prohibition (what is permitted or forbidden)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that one witness is enough for every case. In money matters and in ordinary confirmation of documents, two are needed. The single-witness rule here works because the question is one of איסור.

phrases.english: One witness is believed in matters of prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אֶחָד נֶאֱמָן בְּאִיסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general rule of evidence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שליח's statement confirms a document, so it needs two witnesses like any קיום שטרות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the גט decides an איסור question, the rule that עד אחד נאמן באיסורין applies, and one שליח is enough.

steps.title: One witness works for doubtful fat, not for a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 5: עד אחד נאמן באיסורין applies only where no prohibition was established, but a married woman has an established איסור, making this a דבר שבערוה that needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could say that one witness is believed about prohibitions only in a case like a piece of fat that may be forbidden חלב or may be permitted שומן, where no prohibition was ever established. Here, though, the woman is established as forbidden as an אשת איש. That makes this a דבר שבערוה, and a דבר שבערוה cannot be proven with fewer than two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 5. It says the rule 'one witness is believed for prohibitions' does not fit a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of cases. With the piece of fat, the doubt started from zero, so nothing was ever established as forbidden. A married woman is firmly established as forbidden to others, and switching that status is a דבר שבערוה, which requires two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness is believed about matters of permitted and forbidden
Forbidden fat
Permitted fat
A prohibition was established (a חזקה of being forbidden)
A matter involving forbidden relationships, which needs two witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not saying one witness is never believed. It accepts that rule, but limits it to cases with no established prohibition.

phrases.english: Say that we say
one witness is believed regarding prohibitions,
such as a piece that may be forbidden fat
or may be permitted fat,
where no prohibition was established;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא אִיתַּחְזַק אִיסּוּרָא דְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ –
phrases.english: but here the prohibition of a married woman was established –
it is a matter of forbidden relations,
and a matter of forbidden relations needs no fewer than two!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמְרִינַן עֵד אֶחָד נֶאֱמָן בְּאִיסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that עד אחד נאמן באיסורין covers the שליח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule works only where no איסור was established; אשת איש is an established איסור and a דבר שבערוה, requiring two witnesses.

steps.title: Document confirmation is only a rabbinic requirement
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי שמעון בן לקיש, signed witnesses count as already examined in court, so by Torah law no קיום is needed. The חכמים added it, and they relaxed it here because of עיגון.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, confirming documents should not be needed at all, like רבי שמעון בן לקיש. He said: witnesses signed on a document are treated as if their testimony was already examined in בית דין. It is only the חכמים who required confirmation, and here, to prevent עיגון, the חכמים were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by moving the whole issue out of Torah law. The confirmation that the שליח provides is only a rabbinic requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the שליח was overturning an established אשת איש status with one witness. But by Torah law the signed גט already proves itself, so the woman is divorced by the document itself. The extra confirmation is only a rabbinic layer, and the חכמים who made it could relax it to help women avoid becoming עגונות.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirming the signatures on a document
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל
Their testimony was examined in court
A woman left 'chained,' unable to remarry

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key idea that lets one שליח be enough in רבא's approach. The requirement being relaxed is rabbinic, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: By right, with confirming documents
too it should not be needed,
phrases.notes: He means no confirmation at all should be needed by Torah law, not even two witnesses.

phrases.english: like רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ –
for רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ said:
witnesses signed on a document

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשׂוּ כְּמִי שֶׁנֶּחְקְרָה עֵדוּתָן בְּבֵית דִּין –
phrases.english: become like those whose testimony was examined in court –
and it is the Rabbis who required it;
and here, because of being left chained,
the Rabbis were lenient with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִין הוּא דִּבְקִיּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת נָמֵי לָא לִיבְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שליח alone overturns an established Torah-level אשת איש status.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law the signed גט proves itself; קיום is rabbinic, so the חכמים could relax it because of עיגון.

steps.title: Is it really a leniency within רבא's approach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its earlier objection, now within רבא's approach: relying on one witness is actually a stringency, because the husband can come and contest it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a leniency? It is a stringency! If you required two witnesses, the husband could not come, contest the גט and invalidate it. With one, the husband can come, contest it and invalidate it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same objection it raised earlier against רבה (step 2), now against רבא's explanation. The wording is repeated because it now applies to a new approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the חכמים were lenient by accepting one שליח. The question is that one witness is weaker, so the husband can challenge the גט and leave the woman worse off. That would make the 'leniency' a harm to her.

keyTerms.meaning: Leniency
Stringency
Contests, challenges

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an accidental repeat of steps 2–3. The גמרא deliberately runs the same question and answer again within רבא's approach.

phrases.english: Is this a leniency?! It is a stringency!
For if you require two for it –

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעֵר וּפָסֵיל לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: the husband cannot come, contest and invalidate it;

phrases.aramaic: חַד – אָתֵי בַּעַל וּמְעַרְעֵר וּפָסֵיל לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: with one – the husband can come, contest and invalidate it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קוּלָּא הוּא?! חוּמְרָא הוּא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of leniency in step 7, repeating the objection of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that accepting one שליח is a leniency for the woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One witness leaves room for the husband to contest and invalidate the גט, which harms her.

steps.title: The שליח is careful because he hands it over publicly
steps.stepSummary: Since the גט is given in front of two or three people, the שליח checks carefully from the start and will not bring a flawed גט, so the husband's challenge is not a real concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the master said: in front of how many does he give it to her? רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא disagree. One said in front of two, and one said in front of three. So from the start the שליח checks carefully and will not bring harm on himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave earlier (step 3), now supporting רבא's approach. The leniency is real, because the risk of the husband contesting is small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליח hands over the גט publicly, in front of two or three people. If it later turned out to be flawed, he would be embarrassed. So he checks everything carefully beforehand, and a successful challenge by the husband is unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: The master said (quoting an earlier teaching)
He is certainly careful
To harm himself

phrases.english: Since the master said:
In front of how many does he give it to her?
רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן and רַבִּי חֲנִינָא disagree;
one said: in front of two,
and one said: in front of three;
from the start he is certainly careful
and will not come to harm himself.
phrases.notes: He doesn't want to be shamed in front of those people if the גט turns out to be flawed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: בִּפְנֵי כַּמָּה נוֹתְנוֹ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8, repeating the answer of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reassurance that the feared outcome is unlikely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One witness exposes the גט to the husband's challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The public handover makes the שליח check carefully, so the leniency stands within רבא's approach.
steps.whatToRemember: Within רבא's approach: one שליח is enough because קיום is only rabbinic, the חכמים relaxed it because of עיגון, and the שליח's careful checking keeps the husband from successfully contesting.

steps.title: Why does רבא not accept רבה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא did not explain the משנה like רבה, who said the reason is to make sure the גט was written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, what is his reason for not saying like רבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question and sets up the next step. It asks why רבא rejected רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the שליח declares בפני נכתב to confirm the גט was written לשמה. רבא gave a different reason, that witnesses are not available for קיום. The גמרא wants to know what was wrong with רבה's reason in רבא's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who says the reason is קיום שטרות
The אמורא who says the reason is לשמה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And רָבָא, what is the reason
that he did not say like רַבָּה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the defense of רבא's approach, the גמרא asks why רבא rejects רבה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבא's reason for not accepting רבה's לשמה explanation

steps.title: The משנה never mentions לשמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה does not say 'written in my presence לשמה'. If the concern were לשמה, the declaration would have to mention it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: does the משנה teach 'it was written in my presence לשמה, it was signed in my presence לשמה'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's answer. He rejects רבה's reason because the wording of the משנה does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal were to confirm the גט was written for this woman, the שליח would need to say so outright. The משנה has him say only 'written and signed in my presence', with no mention of לשמה. So לשמה cannot be the reason behind the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (in the משנה)
It was written in my presence
For her sake, specifically for this woman

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Does it teach: 'It was written in my presence for her sake,
it was signed in my presence for her sake'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מִי קָתָנֵי בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's declaration does not mention לשמה, so לשמה cannot be its purpose.

steps.title: Why רבה's view does not require saying 'לשמה'
steps.stepSummary: רבה agrees the declaration should really mention לשמה. It was left out because a longer formula would lead the שליח to shorten it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבה answer? By right the משנה should teach it that way. But if you make the שליח's statement longer, he will come to cut it short.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבה's answer to the challenge from Step 11, which asked why the declaration doesn't say 'לשמה' if that is the concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה admits that the ideal wording would include לשמה. The חכמים kept the formula short on purpose. A long statement is easy to shorten or get wrong, and that could cause problems with the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: By right / strictly speaking, it should be so
You make the statement longer
To cut it short / trim it

phrases.english: And Rabba?
phrases.notes: This means: how would רבה answer the question just asked in Step 11?

phrases.english: By right it should teach it this way,
but if you make his statement longer for him,
he will come to cut it short.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה? בְּדִין הוּא דְּלִיתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבה against רבא's wording challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern explains why the ideal wording was not used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the reason is לשמה, the declaration must say 'לשמה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word was left out so the formula stays short and the שליח won't trim it.

steps.title: Even the current formula could get shortened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the formula as it stands now could also get shortened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, he will come to cut it short!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's answer. Even the present wording, 'written in my presence and signed in my presence,' could be shortened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is that a שליח trims long statements, that worry exists even now. He might say only one half. So the fear of shortening does not seem to explain why לשמה was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Now / as things are
Also / too
He will come (to do something)

phrases.english: Now too he will come to cut it short!
phrases.notes: 'Now' means with the formula as it already is: 'written in my presence, signed in my presence.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי אָתֵי לְמִגְזְּיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that a longer statement would be shortened
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The risk of shortening exists even with the current two-part formula, so it can't be the reason for leaving out לשמה.

steps.title: People drop one of three, not one of two
steps.stepSummary: A person tends to drop one word out of three, but he won't drop one out of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: One out of three he cuts; one out of two he does not cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. A three-part phrase gets shortened, but a two-part phrase does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בפני נכתב לשמה' has three parts, so the שליח might drop 'לשמה'. 'בפני נכתב' has only two parts, and he won't shorten it. So the current formula is safe, and adding לשמה would not be.

keyTerms.meaning: One out of three
He cuts / trims
Out of two

phrases.english: One out of three he cuts,
phrases.notes: For example, from 'written, in my presence, for her sake' he might drop 'for her sake.'

phrases.english: one out of two he does not cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מִתְּלָת גָּאֵיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a two-part and a three-part phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any formula, even the current one, risks being shortened.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a three-part phrase gets trimmed. The two-part phrases 'בפני נכתב' and 'בפני נחתם' stay whole.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה holds the real concern is לשמה. 'לשמה' is not said out loud only to keep the phrase short enough that the שליח won't trim it.

steps.title: Why didn't רבה explain like רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns around and asks why רבה did not accept רבא's reason, that witnesses for קיום are hard to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה, what is the reason he did not say like רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Now it asks what pushed רבה away from רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10-14 asked why רבא rejected רבה's view. Now the question goes the other way. The answer will come from the exact wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Like רבא
The אמורא who says the concern is לשמה

phrases.english: And Rabba, what is the reason
that he did not say like Rava?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 10, now asking about רבה instead of רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness does רבה see in רבא's explanation?

steps.title: 'Written in my presence' points to לשמה
steps.stepSummary: If the issue were only קיום, saying 'signed in my presence' would be enough. Adding 'written in my presence' shows the concern is לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: If so, let it teach 'it was signed in my presence' and nothing more. Why do I need 'it was written in my presence'? Learn from this that we need לשמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבה's reason. The words 'written in my presence' only make sense if the concern is about how the גט was written, meaning לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיום is about confirming signatures, so 'signed in my presence' would cover רבא's concern completely. The extra phrase 'written in my presence' must have its own purpose. That purpose is making sure the גט was written for this woman.

keyTerms.meaning: It was signed in my presence
It was written in my presence
And nothing more
Learn from this / conclude from it
For her sake; the גט must be written for this specific woman

phrases.english: He would tell you:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן נִיתְנֵי ״בְּפָנַי נֶחְתַּם״ וְתוּ לָא;
phrases.english: If so, let it teach 'it was signed in my presence' and nothing more;
why do I need 'it was written in my presence'?
Learn from this that we need it to be for her sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִם כֵּן נִיתְנֵי ״בְּפָנַי נֶחְתַּם״ וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבא's view, 'written in my presence' would be unnecessary. Its presence in the משנה shows the concern is לשמה.

steps.title: רבא: Avoiding confusion with ordinary קיום
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees 'signed in my presence' would be enough by itself. 'Written in my presence' was added so people won't think one witness can do קיום for regular documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? By right it should teach it that way. But if so, people would come to confuse it with קיום of ordinary documents, and think it can be done with one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's defense. 'Written in my presence' is there to keep people from making a mistake about other documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally קיום of a document needs two witnesses. If the שליח said only 'signed in my presence,' it would sound like regular קיום done by one witness, and people would copy that for other documents. Adding 'written in my presence' makes this case look different, so no one learns the wrong rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To get mixed up / confuse
Confirming the signatures on documents
Of the world, meaning ordinary or general
One witness

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying 'written in my presence' adds anything about לשמה. For him it is only a signal that this case is special, so it won't be confused with regular קיום.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this, each אמורא has a way to explain every word of the משנה by his own reason. Next, רבה challenges this answer (step 18), and רבא defends it (step 19).

phrases.english: And Rava?
phrases.notes: This means: how would רבא answer רבה's question from Step 16?

phrases.english: By right it should teach it this way,
but if so,
people will come to confuse it with the confirming of ordinary documents,
thinking it can be done with one witness.
phrases.notes: Regular documents need two witnesses to confirm them. The worry is that people would think one is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא? בְּדִין הוּא דְּלִיתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא against רבה's inference in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra wording guards against a mistaken conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Written in my presence' only makes sense if the concern is לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבא, 'written in my presence' is there so people won't think one witness can confirm ordinary documents.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: 'written in my presence' is added only to keep people from thinking one witness can do קיום for ordinary documents. רבה challenges this in the next step, and step 19 defends it.

steps.title: רבה: A גט and ordinary documents are too different to confuse
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects רבא's worry. A גט and regular documents work so differently that nobody would learn from one to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה would say: Are they even comparable? There, with ordinary documents, the witnesses say 'we know.' Here, with a גט, the שליח says 'in my presence.' There, a woman is not believed. Here, a woman is believed. There, an interested party is not believed. Here, an interested party is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה did not accept רבא's point that 'written in my presence' was added so people would not think one witness can do קיום for regular documents. רבה lists three differences that keep anyone from mixing up the two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's worry was that people would see one person confirm a גט and copy that for ordinary documents. רבה says the rules are already so different that nobody would make that connection. The wording is different ('in my presence' versus 'we know'), and a גט accepts a woman and an interested party, while ordinary documents accept neither.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (a challenge that two cases are not alike)
'We know' (the standard wording witnesses use to confirm signatures on a document)
'In my presence' (the special wording used for a גט)
An interested party, someone with a personal stake in the case
Believed, trusted as testimony

steps.confusionAlert: Who is the 'interested party' here? It is the woman herself. She can bring her own גט and be believed, even though she clearly gains from it.

phrases.english: And רבה: are they comparable?!
There, 'we know'; here, 'in my presence';
there, a woman is not believed,
here, a woman is believed;
there, an interested party is not believed,
here, an interested party is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's reason from step 17 that the extra wording prevents confusion with ordinary קיום.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's claim that people would confuse קיום of a גט with קיום of ordinary documents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two systems differ in three clear ways (wording, a woman's believability, an interested party's believability), so no one would mix them up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in step 17 that 'בפני נכתב' was added so people would not confuse a גט with ordinary קיום שטרות done by one witness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט and ordinary documents already differ in wording ('בפני' versus 'ידעינן'), in a woman's believability, and in an interested party's believability. Nobody would learn one from the other, so רבא's worry about confusion has no basis.

steps.title: רבא: A גט would also work with 'we know,' so confusion is real
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a גט would still be accepted with the ordinary 'we know' wording. So people really could mix it up with ordinary documents and think one witness is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would say to you: Do you mean that here, with a גט, if they say 'we know,' they are not believed? They are believed! And since they are believed when they say 'we know,' people will mix it up with ordinary documents and do קיום with one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his reason against רבה's list of differences. He argues that the first difference, the wording, does not really separate the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said ordinary documents use 'we know' and a גט uses 'in my presence.' רבא points out that a גט confirmed with 'we know' would also be valid, so the wording overlaps. Once the cases look alike, people could think one witness saying 'we know' is enough for any document. That is why 'written in my presence' was added, to make the גט case stand out.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you mean that...? (a rhetorical question that pushes back)
To mix up, to confuse one case with another
Ordinary documents (not a גט)
One witness

steps.whatToRemember: רבה says the extra wording is about לשמה. רבא says it is about קיום and keeping people from wrongly accepting one witness for ordinary documents. Each one defends his view against the other.

phrases.english: And רבא would say to you:
Do you mean that here, when they say 'we know,'
they are not believed?!
And since, when they say 'we know,' they are believed,
people will come to confuse it
with the קיום of ordinary documents, using one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: אַטּוּ הָכָא כִּי אָמְרִי ״יָדְעִינַן״ מִי לָא מְהֵימְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's reason (step 17) against רבה's list of differences (step 18).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording difference is not a real separation, because 'we know' works for a גט too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The different wording ('we know' versus 'in my presence') keeps the two cases apart, so no confusion could happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט may also be confirmed with 'we know,' so the cases overlap. The confusion is a real risk, which justifies the added wording.

steps.title: According to רבה, which תנא requires writing לשמה and more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question. If רבה's reason is about לשמה, which תנא holds that the writing must be לשמה and also requires something else? The text breaks off mid-question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבה, who said the reason is that people are not experts in לשמה: who is this תנא who requires the writing to be לשמה, and also requires...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question about רבה's view. It wants to know which תנא's opinion matches רבה's reason. The rest of the question continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the declaration exists because of לשמה. So the גמרא wants to find which תנא requires the writing of the גט to be לשמה and also requires something more. Identifying that תנא will test whether רבה's reason fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts, people who know the rules well
For her sake, written specifically for this woman
A sage of the משנה period
The writing (of the גט)

phrases.english: And according to רבה, who said
'because they are not experts in לשמה,'
who is this תנא
who requires the writing to be לשמה, and requires

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּה דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ מַאן הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה/רבא back-and-forth and starts a new question about which תנא matches רבה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא requires the writing of a גט to be לשמה and also requires a further condition, matching רבה's reading of the משנה.
